capture.final_message:
Use the Carathéodory splitting identity as the central mechanism.

For the first conjunct, apply the Carathéodory property of \(s_1\) to
\[
A=t\cap(s_1\cup s_2).
\]
The disjointness assumption \(s_1\cap s_2\subseteq\varnothing\) gives the set identities
\[
A\cap s_1=t\cap s_1,\qquad A\setminus s_1=t\cap s_2.
\]
Substituting these into the Carathéodory identity for \(A\) yields the desired additivity.

For the second conjunct, unfold `OuterMeasure.IsCaratheodory`. One implication is precisely the stated inequality (indeed, the defining equality). Conversely, outer-measure subadditivity applied to
\[
t=(t\cap s)\cup(t\setminus s)
\]
always gives
\[
m(t)\le m(t\cap s)+m(t\setminus s).
\]
Combining this with the assumed reverse inequality gives equality, hence the Carathéodory condition. The only auxiliary goals needed are the elementary set identities above and antisymmetry in `ENNReal`.
